title: Minimal deformation retract of a quasicategory
statement: Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ as in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and use quasicategories, simplicial products, equivalence edges, coherent functors and functor equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $C$ be any $\mathcal U'$-small quasicategory, with no local-smallness assumption. For $n\geq0$, put $\partial\Delta^n=\bigcup_{k=0}^n d_k\Delta^{n-1}$, with $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. Two simplices $f,g:\Delta^n\to C$ with the same boundary $b$ are homotopic relative to that boundary if there is a simplicial map $H:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to C$ with endpoints $f,g$, restriction $b\circ\operatorname{pr}_1$ on $\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$, and with $H|_{\{v\}\times\Delta^1}$ an equivalence edge for every vertex $v$ of $\Delta^n$. A quasicategory is minimal if any such pair of simplices is equal, including $n=0$. There exist a simplicial subset $M\subseteq C$ which is a minimal quasicategory, its inclusion $i:M\to C$, and a simplicial retraction $r:C\to M$ with $ri=\mathrm{id}_M$, together with a coherent natural equivalence $\mathrm{id}_C\simeq ir$ constant on $M$. In particular $i$ and $r$ are inverse functor equivalences. The empty quasicategory is allowed.
